title: Kafka decode failures are silently dropped: no DLT, no retry, no operator visibility
actual: BaseKafkaConsumer.decodeContained() catches every decode exception, logs at ERROR and returns null; the caller then returns without invoking the handler, so the record is ack-skipped. A handler exception, by contrast, DOES propagate to the container error handler (DefaultErrorHandler + DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer, FixedBackOff(1000ms, 3 retries)). KafkaProperties.Retry (backoff-ms, max-attempts) is documented 'INTENTIONALLY UNUSED' - the real retry policy is hardcoded in BaseKafkaListenerConfig.
expected: A malformed or poison record must be routed to the DLQ (or at minimum surfaced as a metric) rather than dropped, so the loss is observable and replayable.
trigger: Any payload that does not bind to the target DTO - schema drift, a producer bug, or corruption.
root_cause: Deliberate 'ack-always poison posture' in the decode path, plus a dead Retry configuration block that operators can tune without effect.
consequences: Silent loss of order / payment / shipping / rating / media events. The offset advances as if the event had been handled; no DLQ entry exists; only a log line records it. A schema-evolution mistake upstream can therefore drop events across the fleet with no alarm.
remediation: Make the decode failure path publish to the DLQ (or throw so the container error handler routes it), and either wire shop.kafka.retry into BaseKafkaListenerConfig or delete the dead block.
regression_test: Unit test: a consumer given a malformed payload must either publish to the DLT topic or raise the error so the container routes it; the offset must not advance as a silent success.

title: Orphaned PENDING orders with no order items can never be reconciled - they accumulate and alert forever
actual: OrderCreateSaga.execute() Step 1 commits a PENDING order row in its own transaction; the order items are only persisted in Step 4. A crash between Step 1 and Step 4 leaves a PENDING order with zero order_items. OrderReconciliationScheduler.reconcile() polls the reservation states, finds an empty list, and calls routeToMixed(order, states, 'no applicable reservations') - no automatic action, ever. The sweep re-selects the same row on every tick (5 minutes) because it is still PENDING and older than the 30-minute cutoff.
expected: An order with no reservation-bearing items is either completed or cancelled automatically, or is explicitly excluded from the sweep.
trigger: Process crash, pod eviction, or unhandled error between the Step 1 commit and the Step 4 commit of the create saga.
root_cause: The saga persists the order before its items, and the reconciler's decision table has no case for 'no applicable reservations'.
consequences: Permanent orphan order rows that grow without bound, a permanently firing reconciliation alert, and a cart that stays populated so the customer can retry into a second order while the first is orphaned.
remediation: Either persist the order items in Step 1 alongside the order, or add a reconciler case that cancels (or garbage-collects) a PENDING order older than the cutoff that has no items and no promotion reservation.
regression_test: Integration test: create a PENDING order with no items, run the reconciler, and assert the order reaches a terminal state instead of staying PENDING.

title: No DLT consumer or replay path exists - a message that exhausts its 3 retries is stranded permanently
actual: BaseKafkaListenerConfig installs a DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer, so a listener that throws 4 times routes its record to <topic>.DLT. A fleet-wide search for DLT / DeadLetter shows no consumer, no replay scheduler and no operator tooling for any DLQ topic.
expected: DLQ entries are surfaced (metric / alert) and replayable after the root cause is fixed.
trigger: A downstream dependency (payment, inventory, promotion, search) is unavailable long enough to exhaust the FixedBackOff(1000ms, 3) retry budget.
root_cause: The DLQ publish side was implemented; the consume/replay side was never built.
consequences: A payment.captured.v1 that fails 3 times is lost forever: the order stays PENDING until the 30-minute reconciler, which polls reservation states - but the reservations were never committed, so it is auto-cancelled. The customer paid and the order is cancelled. The same loss applies to shipping.delivered (the order never reaches DELIVERED) and to rating/media lifecycle events.
remediation: Add a DLQ consumer per topic that persists the failure for operator replay, or at minimum a metric plus an alert and a documented manual replay procedure using kafka-console-consumer.
regression_test: Integration test: force a listener to fail 4 times, assert the record lands in the DLQ, then run the replay path and assert the message is processed.

title: auto-offset-reset=latest in every Kafka consumer service: events published while a group has no member are skipped
actual: Every service that consumes Kafka sets shop.kafka.consumer.auto-offset-reset: latest. The shared default in common-kafka KafkaProperties.ConsumerConfig is also 'earliest', but every service overrides it to latest. With 'latest', a consumer group with no committed offsets (a new group, or a group whose offsets were expired) starts at the END of the topic and never sees the backlog.
expected: At-least-once delivery semantics where a consumer group that was down replays the events it missed, which is the premise of the documented 'at-least-once message delivery with recovery mechanisms' claim.
trigger: A consumer service is scaled to zero, redeployed with a new group id, has its offsets expired, or starts after events were published.
root_cause: latest was chosen to avoid replaying the whole topic on a first deployment, without considering the missed-event window.
consequences: Silent event loss. A shipping.delivered event published during a notification-service restart is never delivered (the order never reaches DELIVERED); a payment.captured.v1 published during an order-service restart is never seen (the order stays PENDING until the reconciler cancels it).
remediation: Set auto-offset-reset to earliest for consumers that need gap-free processing, and ensure every consumer group has durable, monitored offsets. Alternatively keep latest but add a reconciliation sweep for every event-driven projection.
regression_test: Integration test: publish an event with no active consumer, start the consumer, and assert the event is processed.

title: The payment-captured confirm gate and the cancel-refund trigger are both DISABLED by default - an order can be confirmed without payment and cancelled without refund
actual: order-service application.yml sets shop.services.payment.enabled: ${PAYMENT_SERVICE_ENABLED:false} with the comment 'payment-captured confirm gate, default off until payment-service ships'. ShopServicesProperties.Service.isEnabled() returns false for that value. OrderServiceImpl.confirmOrder() only calls paymentClient.findCapturedByOrderId() when paymentClient.isEnabled() is true, so with the default configuration the confirm path never verifies that a payment exists. PaymentServiceClient.refundByOrderId() returns true immediately when the client is disabled, so the admin-cancel path reports success without issuing a refund. payment-service IS shipped (Stripe, COD, VNPay, MoMo providers, webhooks, refunds), so the 'until payment-service ships' premise no longer holds.
expected: An order is CONFIRMED only when a CAPTURED payment exists; cancelling a CONFIRMED order always triggers a refund.
trigger: A deployment that does not set PAYMENT_SERVICE_ENABLED=true - which is the shipped default and the value in .env.example style configuration.
root_cause: A feature flag introduced during an MVP phase was never flipped once the downstream shipped, and its default is the unsafe value.
consequences: Two money-critical invariants are silently unenforced in the default deployment: (1) an order reaches CONFIRMED with no captured payment - the customer receives goods that were never paid for; (2) an admin cancel of a CONFIRMED order marks it CANCELLED while the customer keeps their money. Neither is visible in logs or metrics.
remediation: Default shop.services.payment.enabled to true, fail the application context at startup when it is false while payment-service is deployed, and make refundByOrderId report a distinct 'skipped' outcome instead of returning true.
regression_test: Integration test: with the payment client enabled, confirmOrder must fail with ORD-4012 when no CAPTURED payment exists. A configuration test must assert the shipped default is not 'false'.

title: Service-to-service client secret defaults to 'changeme' in order-service
actual: shop.services.keycloak.client-secret: ${ORDER_SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET:changeme}. The value is used for the client_credentials token request that authenticates order-service to inventory, promotion and payment.
expected: No credential default in a shipped configuration; the service must fail fast when the secret is absent.
trigger: A deployment that does not set ORDER_SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET.
root_cause: Developer placeholder left in the shipped default.
consequences: Either the service fails to authenticate (availability) or, if the Keycloak client is created with the same 'changeme' secret, any party that knows the literal can mint SERVICE-role tokens for order-service and call the confirm, ship, deliver, cancel and verify-purchase endpoints directly.
remediation: Remove the default and validate at startup; rotate the realm client secret.
regression_test: Configuration test asserting the shipped default is absent and the context fails to start without the secret.

title: A partial Stripe refund is recorded as a full refund: the webhook reads the charge amount, not the refunded amount
actual: STRIPE_EVENT_STATUS maps charge.refunded to REFUNDED. toCarrierPayload() reads data.object.amount and converts minor -> major units, then process() compares it against payment.getAmount() and only accepts an exact match. For a Stripe charge.refunded event, data.object is the Charge whose 'amount' field is the ORIGINAL charge amount and whose 'amount_refunded' field carries the refunded total. A partial refund therefore passes the amount check and the payment row transitions CAPTURED -> REFUNDED.
expected: A partial refund must not mark the payment fully refunded; the refunded amount must be reconciled against the captured amount.
trigger: Any partial refund at Stripe (a common support scenario: shipping cost, partial return).
root_cause: The webhook maps a Stripe event type to a single terminal fleet status without reading the refunded amount.
consequences: The local payment is marked REFUNDED although only part of the money came back. Order, revenue and refund reporting then over-state refunds, and no further refund can be issued because the state machine only allows CAPTURED -> REFUNDED.
remediation: Read amount_refunded for charge.refunded, compare it against the captured amount, and only transition to REFUNDED on a full refund; introduce a PARTIALLY_REFUNDED status (or record the refunded amount) otherwise.
regression_test: Unit test: a charge.refunded event with amount_refunded < charge amount must not transition the payment to REFUNDED.

title: Payment create idempotency replays without validating that the request payload matches
actual: create() looks up repository.findByIdempotencyKeyAndUserId(idempotencyKey, userId) and returns the existing Payment via existing.orElseGet(...). It never compares orderId, amount or currency against the incoming request. order-service solves the same problem with a requestHash guard (IdempotencyServiceImpl.resolve).
expected: Reusing an idempotency key with a different payload must be rejected with a conflict, not silently return the previous payment.
trigger: A caller reuses an idempotency key across two different orders or amounts - for example a client-side retry bug or a multi-tenant key collision.
root_cause: The idempotency lookup checks identity but not intent.
consequences: The caller believes it created a payment for order B and receives the payment object for order A. The order B payment never exists, so the later capture targets the wrong payment; the confirm gate for order B then fails closed and order B is auto-cancelled by the reconciler.
remediation: Store a request hash on the payment row (or a separate idempotency table) and reject a key reuse whose payload differs, matching the order-service pattern.
regression_test: Integration test: creating a payment with the same idempotency key but a different amount must fail with PAYMENT_DUPLICATE_REQUEST.

title: The confirm-path payment gate inspects only the first page of payments for an order
actual: findCapturedByOrderId() calls GET /api/v1/payments?orderId=... with no size parameter and then filters the returned page for a CAPTURED payment with findFirst(). The controller's default page size is 10 (PageableConstant.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE).
expected: The gate must evaluate all payments for the order, or the endpoint must expose a dedicated captured-payment lookup.
trigger: An order with more than ten payment records - for example a client that retries payment creation across several providers or a partially failed checkout.
root_cause: A paged collection endpoint is used as a lookup.
consequences: The gate fails closed (ORD-4012) even though a captured payment exists beyond the first page, so the order can never be confirmed and is later auto-cancelled - a paid customer loses the order.
remediation: Add a dedicated payment-service endpoint such as GET /api/v1/payments/by-order/{orderId}/captured, or pass an explicit large page size and page through the results.
regression_test: Integration test: create 12 payments for one order where only the last is CAPTURED; the gate must find it.

title: Webhook signature verifier returns HTTP 500 (not 401) for a malformed 64-character v1 hex value
actual: In the Stripe-style branch, parseStripeHeader() only validates that v1 has length 64, then verifyInternal() calls HexFormat.of().parseHex(stripe.v1Hex) with no try/catch. HexFormat.parseHex throws IllegalArgumentException for a non-hexadecimal string of the correct length. The legacy bare-hex branch DOES wrap parseHex in a try/catch and returns false.
expected: A malformed signature must be rejected as an invalid signature (401 PAY-5005), never as an unhandled server error.
trigger: An unauthenticated caller posts a webhook with a 64-character non-hex v1 component.
root_cause: Inconsistent error handling between the two verification branches.
consequences: An unauthenticated request can provoke a 500 with a stack trace instead of a clean 401. It pollutes error budgets and alerting, and the error path is reachable without authentication.
remediation: Validate the hex charset in parseStripeHeader (or wrap the parseHex call) and return false so the caller raises WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.
regression_test: Unit test: verify() with a 64-character non-hex v1 must return false rather than throw.

title: Admin cancel of a SHIPPED order marks it CANCELLED with no refund and no restock, while the inline comment claims SHIPPED is terminal for everyone
actual: OrderStatusServiceImpl.ALLOWED permits SHIPPED -> CANCELLED (H12). OrderServiceImpl.cancelOrder() only handles the PENDING branch (release reservations + release the promotion) and the CONFIRMED+admin branch (releaseCommitted + refund). A SHIPPED order falls through both branches: the status is set to CANCELLED and publishCancelled is emitted, with no refund, no stock movement and no return record.
expected: Either SHIPPED -> CANCELLED is rejected, or it is routed to the return/refund flow that the H12 comment intends for post-shipment cancellations.
trigger: An administrator cancels a shipped order (carrier issue, fraud chargeback, recall).
root_cause: The state machine was widened for admin tooling but the cancel workflow was not widened with it.
consequences: The order reads CANCELLED to the customer while the goods are in transit and the customer keeps their money; no return or refund record is created, so the refund is never driven by the platform.
remediation: Route the SHIPPED -> CANCELLED path into OrderReturnService (the return/refund flow that already exists), or remove the transition from the state machine.
regression_test: Integration test: cancelling a SHIPPED order must either fail with ORDER_INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION or create a return record and trigger a refund.

title: Reservation release during compensation is best-effort and the failure is swallowed after the order row is deleted, orphaning the stock hold
actual: OrderCreateSaga.releaseAllReservations() catches every exception and only logs it. The saga then deletes the order row. OrderServiceImpl.releaseAllReservationsById() and releaseAllCommittedReservationsById() behave the same way. Once the order row is gone, no row references the reservation, so the order-service reconciler cannot find it; the only recovery is inventory-service's TTL sweep, which releases the hold after inventory.reservation-ttl-seconds (default 900).
expected: A compensation failure leaves a durable, discoverable record linking the orphaned reservation to the order.
trigger: inventory-service is unavailable or returns an error while the saga is compensating.
root_cause: Compensation is fire-and-forget and the durable link (the order row) is destroyed immediately afterwards.
consequences: Stock stays unavailable for up to 15 minutes after a failed checkout, with no alert beyond a log line. Under a partial outage the effective sellable stock is materially lower than the ledger says.
remediation: Record compensation failures (a failed_compensation table or an outbox row) before deleting the order, and have the reconciler retry them.
regression_test: Integration test: force the inventory release to fail during saga compensation and assert a durable compensation record exists that the reconciler can retry.

title: cancelOrder holds a database transaction open across several remote HTTP calls
actual: cancelOrder() is annotated @Transactional and calls stockReservationService.release(...) per item, promotionClient.release(...), promotionClient.releaseCommitted(...) and paymentClient.refundByOrderId(...) - each a remote HTTP call with a 3-5 second timeout - all inside the open transaction. The order row update and the outbox event are written at the end of the same transaction.
expected: Remote calls run outside the transaction; the local state change and its outbox event commit in a short transaction.
trigger: A slow downstream during a cancellation.
root_cause: The cancel workflow mixes remote orchestration with the local transaction.
consequences: A pooled DB connection is held for the sum of the downstream latencies. With Hikari maximum-pool-size=20, a burst of cancellations against a degraded inventory or payment service can exhaust the pool and stall unrelated requests on the same service.
remediation: Split the cancel workflow: read the order, perform the remote releases outside a transaction, then commit the status change plus outbox event in a short transaction (the same shape the confirm path already uses).
regression_test: Concurrency test: hold the inventory service at 2s per call and assert the order-service connection pool is not exhausted by concurrent cancels.

title: mergeCart lets any authenticated user claim any guest cart by guessing its id
actual: POST /api/v1/carts/merge is authenticated but takes guestCartId as a free query parameter and derives the guest user id as UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("guest:" + guestCartId). There is no check that the guest cart was created by the caller.
expected: A guest cart may only be merged by a caller who proves possession of the guest cart id, or the merge must be scoped to carts that were created for that browser session.
trigger: An authenticated user submits another user's guestCartId to /api/v1/carts/merge.
root_cause: The guest cart id is treated as a public identifier rather than a capability token.
consequences: A guest cart's contents can be claimed by an unrelated account. Impact is limited because a guest cart holds only product selections, but it breaks the guest-to-account handoff contract and can pollute another user's cart.
remediation: Treat the guest cart id as a capability: require it to be presented in a header that matches the cart's creation record, and/or rate-limit and audit merge attempts.
regression_test: Integration test: merging a guest cart id that the caller did not create must be rejected.

title: Consumer group ids are inconsistent: one order-service listener relies on the default group id
actual: PaymentLifecycleConsumer declares an explicit groupId 'order-service-payment-group'. ShippingDeliveredConsumer declares no groupId and therefore inherits shop.kafka.consumer.group-id = 'order-service'. Two listeners in the same service can therefore share a consumer group, in which case Kafka assigns each partition to only one member and each message is delivered to exactly one of them.
expected: Every listener in a service has an explicit, distinct consumer group id.
trigger: A second listener is added to order-service without an explicit group id.
root_cause: Mixed convention - some listeners pin a group id, others rely on the shared default.
consequences: Adding one more listener can silently halve the delivery of an existing topic; the shipping.delivered event may stop reaching order-service entirely.
remediation: Give every @KafkaListener an explicit groupId and add a static test that fails when a listener has no explicit group.
regression_test: Static test: assert every production @KafkaListener declares groupId.

title: Order tracking is unauthenticated and gated only by the order phone number
actual: shop.security.public-paths includes '/api/v1/orders/track'. trackOrder(orderId, phoneNumber) loads the order and compares the phone number with equalsIgnoreCase, then returns the recipient name, shipping address, total, status and every line item.
expected: Order tracking should require an authenticated owner, or at minimum a non-guessable token in addition to the phone number.
trigger: An attacker with an order id and a guessable or leaked phone number calls the public endpoint.
root_cause: A mutable, low-entropy attribute is used as the sole authorisation factor on an unauthenticated endpoint.
consequences: Disclosure of the recipient name, the full shipping address and the order value - personal data - to anyone who can guess the phone number or who has obtained it from a previous breach or a shared device.
remediation: Require authentication for tracking, or add a per-order tracking token delivered at checkout, and keep only the phone number as a secondary confirmation factor.
regression_test: Security test: the tracking endpoint must reject an unauthenticated request even with the correct phone number, unless an explicit tracking token is supplied.
